summary: 47-ft cast-iron watchtower in Marcus Garvey Park, built 1855-57, NRHP 1976; disassembled 2014, restored, reopened 2019; standing and public.

facts.design: Cast-iron fire watchtower; design by James Bogardus, built by Julius H. Kroehl
facts.agency: New York City Department of Parks and Recreation

access.note: In Marcus Garvey Park. The tower reopened to visitors in December 2019. A 2019 NYC Parks event offered ranger-led visits inside. No source describes a general climbing rule today.

events.note: Build dates differ: Wikipedia infobox 1855-1857, Conservancy 1855-56, Wikidata inception 1856. The tower went into service in 1857.
Went into service in response to Harlem residents' demand (Wikipedia).
Designated a New York City landmark (Wikipedia gives July 12, 1967).
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, date published June 21, 1976 (NPGallery).
Designated on the New York State Register of Historic Places, June 23, 1980 (Wikipedia).
NYC Parks disassembled the tower starting in late 2014, piece by piece, and sent it out of state for restoration.
Reopened to visitors in December 2019. Wikipedia's infobox gives 'Restored in 2020'. The NYC Parks event of December 2019 calls it recently restored.

corrections.why: The NRHP record lists the county as New York County. Manhattan is a borough of that county.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's infobox gives 1855-1857, the Conservancy gives 1855-56, and Wikidata gives 1856 as inception. The timeline uses 1856 and the text gives the range.
Wikipedia's infobox says 'Restored in 2020', but its text says the tower reopened in December 2019, and the NYC Parks event of December 2019 calls it recently restored. The timeline uses 2019.

notes_for_editor: The NYT article (2019-10-25) and the NYC Parks press release returned HTTP 403, so neither was used. The NRHP nomination PDF is not digitized in NPGallery. The NYC Parks event page is a web.archive.org copy. The 6sqft and Untapped Cities search hits were not read. Staffing is described only as volunteers in the 1850s. Only the 1980 NYS register date comes from Wikipedia alone.
